mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates robust labor market conditions and rising consumer spending, which supports corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in 60% or more of periods when PAYEMS increases by at least 100k over the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.0%, it signals a tight labor market that typically precedes stronger economic activity and corporate profit growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in 60% or more of instances where UNRATE is below 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: The joint increase in consumer spending (RSAFS) and industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a synchronized expansion in demand and supply, which typically results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The correlation between the joint signal (RSAFS and INDPRO both rising) and positive SPX 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p>0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%), a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals an economic slowdown, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS>4.0%), INDPRO declines are associated with positive SPX 20-day returns in 60% or more of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) reflects strong manufacturing activity and economic expansion, which typically supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in 60% or more of periods when INDPRO increases by at least 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) rises above 4.5%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in 60% or more of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: In housing boom regimes (HOUST > 1300 thousand units), rising consumer spending (RSAFS) indicates strong household demand and economic momentum, which typically drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: During housing boom regimes (HOUST>1300), RSAFS increases are associated with negative SPX 20-day returns in 60% or more of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100 (index 2017=100), it signals a contraction in manufacturing output and economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in 60% or more of periods when INDPRO declines below 100.
